title: Hosted: enable hardware profile pack for small canary cohort (feature flag) + kill switch rollback
author: Rafael Mendes
description: Summary: This PR wires the new hardware tuning profile pack into Hosted behind a feature flag and rolls it out to a small canary cohort. It also adds a kill switch and a deterministic rollback path that reverts hosts to pre-pack defaults without requiring a runtime binary rollback. Motivation: We need a safe, observable path to enable the profile pack defaults in Hosted while protecting p99 latency and error budgets under mixed workloads. This is a prerequisite for the runtime-1.22 release train and the broader Dedicated/Private opt-in story. Changes: (1) Add Hosted-scoped feature flag `runtime.profile_pack.enabled` with default OFF. (2) Add canary cohort selector (region + pool + instance type guardrails) so we can enable on a targeted slice. (3) Add kill switch `runtime.profile_pack.kill_switch` that forces legacy defaults even if the enable flag is ON, and propagates within ~60s via config refresh. (4) Implement safe rollback semantics: when kill switch is activated, runtime logs a single-line "PROFILE_PACK_DISABLED_BY_KILL_SWITCH" event, exports a counter, and reverts to legacy scheduler/batching defaults while retaining profile_id/profile_version tags as `none` for clarity. (5) Add audit log hooks for flag flips (who/when/what scope) and include active flag state in `/health` debug bundle (requested by on-call). (6) Tighten guardrails: if the detected GPU SKU is unknown or driver/CUDA combo is outside the compatibility matrix, the runtime refuses to enable the pack and records `profile_pack_compat_refused_total{reason=...}`; the host remains on legacy defaults. Flag behavior details: `enabled=false` -> legacy behavior (no profile selection). `enabled=true` + `kill_switch=false` -> profile pack selection applies at startup and on model load. `enabled=true` + `kill_switch=true` -> force legacy behavior (explicit override). Canary targeting: Initial cohort is 1% of Hosted traffic, limited to `us-east-1` + `eu-west-1` H100 pools, excluding any MIG pools. Selection is enforced by control-plane tags `hosted.canary_profile_pack=true` (set by Fleet Ops) and verified in runtime by reading host labels at startup (fail closed to legacy). Rollback path: (a) Flip kill switch ON at global Hosted scope; (b) confirm counters and logs; (c) optionally flip `enabled` OFF after stability. Rollback does not require draining or restarting pods, but we recommend restarting long-lived pods within 24h to ensure a clean slate for selection state. Observability: Adds metrics `profile_pack_enabled` (gauge), `profile_pack_kill_switch_enabled` (gauge), `profile_pack_compat_refused_total` (counter with reason label), and `profile_pack_rollout_events_total` (counter). Also adds a structured log at startup with `profile_pack_state` and `canary_cohort` fields. Testing: Unit tests for precedence (kill switch overrides enabled), config refresh behavior, and refusal behavior on incompatible hardware. Staging run: enabled on `hosted-staging` for 24h with no p95/p99 regression observed on mixed prompt bucket canaries; dashboards linked below. Monitoring / runbook notes: On-call should watch `scheduler_queue_ms` p95/p99, `kernel_choice` distribution changes, error rates (429/5xx), and `profile_pack_compat_refused_total` spikes (indicates fleet drift or bad canary tagging). Related: ENG-4933 rollout plan, ENG-4930 perf-canary gating, ENG-4931 observability tagging, INT-8831 debug bundle request. Follow-ups: (1) Add automatic canary expansion gating via perf-canary once stable for 48h. (2) Document kill switch semantics in Confluence rollout checklist. (3) Add separate kill switch for B200 bring-up (do not enable by default).

review_conversation: Sean Gallagher: Can we guarantee kill switch propagates without a deploy? I want an explicit statement on config refresh interval + a metric we can watch during rollback.

Rafael Mendes (author): Yes—Hosted control-plane refreshes runtime flags every 30s (worst-case 60s due to jitter). Added gauges `profile_pack_kill_switch_enabled` and `profile_pack_enabled` so we can confirm adoption before declaring rollback complete.
Neha Kapoor: Please ensure we fail closed if the canary tag is missing or host labels can’t be read. We can’t afford accidental broader enablement.

Rafael Mendes (author): Updated gating to require `hosted.canary_profile_pack=true`; if labels unavailable or mismatched -> legacy defaults. Added `profile_pack_rollout_events_total{event="cohort_mismatch"}` to make this visible.
Sofia Ivanova: When kill switch flips, are we reverting scheduler knobs only, or also profile-derived concurrency/batching? We need deterministic behavior to triage p99.

Rafael Mendes (author): Kill switch forces the entire profile-pack path off (selection + application). Runtime uses legacy scheduler/batching defaults and logs the explicit disable event. Clarified in description and added a unit test for it.
Allison Grant: Metric label cardinality: don’t label refusal with full driver strings; please bucket reasons.
Rafael Mendes (author): Ack—`reason` label is now an enum bucket (unknown_sku, cuda_too_old, driver_too_old, mig_enabled, missing_host_labels). No raw versions in labels.
Connor O'Brien: Please add a release note blurb for runtime-1.22. This is a behavior change even if behind a flag.
Rafael Mendes (author): Added an internal release note snippet to the PR description and flagged ENG-4934 for the formal release note entry.
release_notes: Hosted: Added feature-flagged rollout support for hardware tuning profile pack with canary cohort targeting and an emergency kill switch. Default remains OFF.
merge_outcome: Merged to main; will be enabled only in hosted-staging immediately and then in a 1% Hosted canary cohort after Fleet Ops tags the target pools.
